context: At every node of a binary search tree, all values in its left subtree are smaller than its own and all values in its right subtree are larger. Edge arrows point from parent to child.

The four-level perfect binary search tree contains nodes 1 through 15. Root 8 has left child 4 and right child 12. The left and right children of 4 are 2 and 6, and those of 12 are 10 and 14. The children of 2 are 1 and 3, those of 6 are 5 and 7, those of 10 are 9 and 11, and those of 14 are 13 and 15, in left-to-right order.
The pointer cur points to the node currently being checked, highlighted in solid blue. Blue arrows and blue rings around nodes mark the search path taken so far.

frames.announcement: Start the search for 7 by pointing cur to root 8.
frames.explanation: Initialize cur to root 8, highlighted in solid blue. Compare target 7 with the current value 8. Since 7 < 8, the target must be in the left subtree, so the next move is down and left to child 4. The path so far is 8.
frames.key_state: The pointer cur points to root 8. Since the target 7 < 8, prepare to move to left child 4.
frames.title: Start at root 8

frames.announcement: Since 7 is less than 8, cur moves from 8 to its left child, 4.
frames.explanation: Since 7 < 8, set cur = cur.left to follow the blue arrow from 8 to left child 4. Compare target 7 with the current value 4. Since 7 > 4, turn next to the right subtree of 4. The path so far is 8→4.
frames.key_state: The pointer cur points to node 4 (path 8→4). Since the target 7 > 4, prepare to move to right child 6.
frames.title: Go left to node 4

frames.announcement: Since 7 is greater than 4, cur moves from 4 to its right child, 6.
frames.explanation: Since 7 > 4, set cur = cur.right to follow the blue arrow from 4 to right child 6. Compare target 7 with the current value 6. Since 7 > 6, continue to the right child of 6. The path so far is 8→4→6.
frames.key_state: The pointer cur points to node 6 (path 8→4→6). Since the target 7 > 6, prepare to move to right child 7.
frames.title: Go right to node 6

frames.announcement: Since 7 is greater than 6, cur moves from 6 to its right child, 7. The target matches, completing the search.
frames.explanation: Since 7 > 6, set cur = cur.right to follow the blue arrow from 6 to right child 7. The value at cur now equals the target 7. Exit the loop and return node 7. The path taken is 8→4→6→7.
frames.key_state: The pointer cur points to target node 7 (path 8→4→6→7). The search succeeds.
frames.title: Find node 7

result: The pointer cur compares four nodes along 8 → 4 → 6 → 7. At the fourth step it finds the target value 7 and returns that node. The search leaves all tree connections intact.
summary: Search for 7 in a binary search tree containing values 1 through 15. At each step, compare values and choose the left or right branch.
title: Searching for node 7 in a binary search tree
